title: Doobie Brothers Singer Reconnects With Son He Placed for Adoption
summary:
One of the Doobie Brothers has reconnected with a long-lost son. Michael McDonald, a singer in the band, made contact a year and a half ago with his biological son, Michael Goessling. Goessling is 59 years old and was adopted as a baby.

Goessling told NBC that he never knew his biological parents until last year. Then he received a letter saying they wanted to meet him. His first conversation with McDonald was over the phone.

"I just said: 'What a voice that guy has!'" Goessling said. "It just sounded so familiar, but I couldn't place it. Finally, I just said: 'Are you Michael McDonald?' And he chuckled and he said, 'Yeah, I'm afraid so.'"

Goessling figured out his birth father's identity after McDonald told him he was a musician with a gig that night.

"There are still days I wake up, and my first thought is I am coming out of the craziest dream, and it's been a year and a half," Goessling added. "I'm still trying to get my head around all of it."

Back when McDonald was 14, he and his middle-school girlfriend put their baby up for adoption. McDonald went on to replace Tom Johnston as the lead singer of the Doobie Brothers. He has five Grammys and helped the band score the Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 "What A Fool Believes,".

Goessling told NBC that he never felt resentment toward his biological parents, who he says are still good friends, for putting him up for adoption. "I just wanted to thank them for the choices they made on my behalf and for giving me a shot in this world, and how grateful I was for that," he said. "They were always heroes in my story."
why_it_matters: It shows how families can find each other years later, and how people can feel thankful for hard choices made long ago.
